title: Comcast's "fiber-powered Wi-Fi" is just cable, AT&T says in false advertising case
gist: AT&T sued Comcast for falsely advertising its hybrid fiber-coaxial Xfinity service as 'fiber-powered', seeking profits restitution and an injunction, mirroring its August suit against Charter. The fight comes as Comcast's broadband losses accelerate (144,000 in Q3 2026) amid low-priced fiber and fixed-wireless competition.

insights.claim: AT&T sued Comcast in US District Court for the Northern District of California, alleging Comcast's marketing of Xfinity cable Internet and Wi-Fi as 'Fiber-Powered' is false advertising violating US and California competition laws.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Fiber marketing is now a litigated competitive battleground between telcos and cable; watch for injunctions that blunt cable's rebranding against fiber.
insights.quote: AT&T on Friday accused Comcast of false advertising in a lawsuit challenging the marketing claim that Comcast’s cable broadband service and Wi-Fi are “fiber-powered.”

insights.claim: AT&T argues Comcast's 'fiber-powered' claim is literally false because the vast majority of Xfinity Internet runs over a hybrid fiber-coaxial (HFC) network whose last-mile connection to the home is copper coaxial cable, not fiber.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: The legal theory hinges on last-mile technology; a win would force cable to differentiate less on 'fiber' and more on price.
insights.quote: the vast majority of Xfinity Internet runs over a hybrid fiber-coaxial (‘HFC’) network, where the critical ‘last mile’ connection to the customer’s home uses copper coaxial cable, not fiber.

insights.claim: AT&T seeks restitution of all profits Comcast earned from the 'fiber-powered' advertising plus a permanent injunction requiring Comcast to stop describing its HFC service as 'Fiber-Powered'.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Potential financial exposure for Comcast beyond marketing changes; the remedy request signals AT&T views the claim as materially diverting subscribers.
insights.locator: “Comcast should be required to restore to AT&T

insights.claim: As a fallback, AT&T asks the court to find Comcast's advertising misleading even if not literally false, because it has the capacity to deceive a substantial segment of consumers into believing Xfinity is delivered over fiber alone.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Two-tier legal argument raises odds of at least partial relief against Comcast's marketing.
insights.locator: AT&T said that even if the court

insights.claim: Comcast cable Internet uses coaxial cable for the final connection to homes, producing upload speeds far slower than download speeds, while fiber-to-the-home can deliver symmetrical upload and download speeds.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Upload asymmetry is a structural product disadvantage for cable vs fiber ISPs, sustaining fiber share gains.
insights.locator: While Comcast has deployed plenty of fiber

insights.claim: Comcast has deployed fiber-to-the-home in only small portions of its cable territory while marketing its service as fiber-powered in most areas where cable makes the final connection.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Comcast's limited FTTH footprint means its competitive response to fiber is largely marketing rather than network upgrade, a risk if marketing is curbed.

insights.claim: Comcast lost 144,000 residential broadband customers in Q3 2026, up from a 91,000-customer loss in Q3 2025, as fiber and fixed wireless competitors take share and Comcast cuts jobs in its cable division.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Accelerating broadband losses are a key bear signal for cable equities and a tailwind for fiber and fixed-wireless providers.
insights.quote: Comcast lost 144,000 residential broadband customers in Q3 2026, up from a 91,000-customer loss in the same quarter a year ago.
insights.locator: Comcast is cutting jobs in its cable division

insights.claim: Comcast co-CEO Mike Cavanagh complained of 'irrational pricing' by competitors, and CFO Jason Armstrong said fiber ISPs offer $30-$40 monthly broadband in some markets despite fiber deployment costing $1,500 or more per home.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Price war pressure on cable ARPU; Comcast management frames fiber pricing as uneconomic, implying they expect it to be unsustainable.
insights.quote: Comcast CFO Jason Armstrong said fiber ISPs are offering $30 to $40 monthly broadband deals in certain markets

insights.claim: Comcast has offered 'fiber-powered Wi-Fi' with speeds up to 300Mbps for $40 a month, matching the low price points it criticizes fiber ISPs for offering.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Shows Comcast is meeting fiber on price at the low end while borrowing fiber branding, compressing broadband margins.

insights.claim: The BBB National Programs' National Advertising Division found in June that Comcast accurately described its cable-and-fiber mix in a disclosure but did not make that disclosure prominent enough, recommending it be more prominent and proximate to the 'fiber-powered' claim; Comcast said it would comply.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Self-regulatory route produced only disclosure tweaks, prompting AT&T to escalate to federal court.
insights.quote: the disclosure should be more prominent or placed closer to the triggering claim

insights.claim: AT&T itself previously marketed 4G LTE as '5GE' or '5G Evolution', which the National Advertising Division found likely to mislead consumers into thinking they had 5G.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Network-labeling disputes are a recurring telecom tactic; AT&T's own history may weaken its moral standing but not its legal claims.
insights.locator: AT&T has its own history of ads

insights.claim: AT&T sued Charter in August in US District Court for the Northern District of Texas over its 'fiber-powered' Spectrum marketing, after Charter modified disclosures following an AT&T NAD complaint in March.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: AT&T is running a coordinated legal campaign against major cable operators' fiber branding; outcomes will set industry-wide marketing norms.
insights.locator: AT&T has a similar ongoing battle against Charter

insights.claim: Charter moved to dismiss in October, arguing its HFC network is 'powered by fiber' in the same sense computers are 'powered by Intel chips,' and that it openly discloses its coaxial connection.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Charter's dismissal motion is the first test of cable's defense; a ruling will signal how the Comcast case may go.
insights.quote: much as computers are ‘powered by Intel chips,’ Charter’s HFC network—and the Internet service it delivers to customers—are powered by fiber
insights.locator: Charter filed a motion to dismiss
